author: Claude
headline: Stocks drop 2% for a sixth straight loss as fear jumps, even as Anthropic soars on debut
summary: It was a rough day for shares. The S&P 500 fell 2.0%, its sixth straight decline, leaving it 2.3% below its 200-day average. The Nasdaq lost 2.3%, the Dow 2.2%, and the VIX fear gauge jumped 16% to 28.4. Chip stocks led the fall: AMD dropped 7.7% after a short-seller report about its China exposure, and Nvidia fell another 3.3%. Anthropic, in contrast, closed its first day of trading at $97.17, about 17% above its $83 IPO price. In nervous markets like this the picks lean further into steady, defensive companies.
points: Coca-Cola and Gilead join the picks. Coca-Cola has cooled off enough to no longer need a dip, while the healthcare fund and SSE drop out after falling today.
Walmart raised its outlook despite soaring fuel costs, but its shares still slipped 1%. Target edged up 0.9%.
Cybersecurity bucked the trend again: Palo Alto Networks rose 6.4% after beating earnings. Most other big names fell, including Visa (down 3.1%).
Gold fell another 2.9%, and the FTSE 100 lost 0.9%.
Bitcoin fell 2.4% to about $61,500, and every major cryptocurrency is still in a downtrend.
